transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because my head just doesn’t stay on task anymore. It's getting pretty frustrating. Like, I’ll be doing inventory at work, or trying to study for this supervisor certification, and I just keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk all the way to the supply closet and completely forget what I even went in there for. I just can't seem to focus my thoughts lately.

{"intent":"Determine when the concentration problems began to distinguish lifelong ADHD from a recent mood, sleep, anxiety, or cognitive change.","question":"When did you first notice these problems with concentration and memory?"]

It's been going on for about three years now. It started right around the time the contractor I work for changed our schedules. They put us on these rotating evening and overnight shifts at the larger properties, and that's when I really started noticing the issues with my focus.
Do your concentration problems become worse during or after your overnight shifts?

Yeah, I'd say it's definitely worse after the overnights. My sleep has been messed up for a long time now. Like, after an overnight shift, I’ll just lie there in bed... I'm so tired, but my brain is just wired. And even on the days when I do manage to sleep a decent number of hours, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all. So yeah, the focus is definitely worse when I'm dealing with that.
Do your sleep and concentration improve when you have several days without overnight or rotating shifts?

Honestly, I'm not really sure. I don't usually get several days off in a row from that schedule to really find out. But even when I do get a regular weekend or a couple of normal days, I haven't noticed much of an improvement. I still wake up feeling just as tired, and my head is still pretty foggy.
Before your work schedule changed, did you have similar problems with concentration or forgetfulness?
No, I really didn't. Before they switched my schedule, I didn't have any trouble getting my work done or remembering what I needed to do. It all just seemed to start when the shifts changed.
When you are able to keep a regular daytime schedule for several days, do you still have difficulty falling asleep at night?

Yeah, like I mentioned a minute ago, my sleep has just been messed up for a long time now. Even if I get a few normal daytime shifts in a row, it doesn't really fix it. I might not be quite as tired but wired as I am right after an overnight shift, but I still struggle to get to sleep. And even when I do manage to drift off and get a decent number of hours at night, I still wake up the next morning feeling like I barely rested at all. It just never really feels like I catch up.
When you are free to sleep on your preferred schedule, without needing to wake for work, does your sleep become restful?

Like I was just saying, not really. It doesn't seem to matter if I don't have an alarm set or anywhere to be. My sleep has just been messed up for a long time now. Even on days where I can sleep on my own schedule and I actually manage to get a decent number of hours in... I still wake up feeling like I barely rested at all. It's like my body is just stuck in that tired but wired mode from the overnights, and sleeping in doesn't really fix it.
When you try to sleep at your intended bedtime, do you feel sleepy but remain unable to fall asleep, or do you mainly not feel sleepy until much later?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, I'm pretty much always exhausted, so I feel like I should be sleepy. But when I actually get in bed... I don't know, I haven't really paid attention to whether I actually feel sleepy right at that moment or if it hits me later. I just know I lay there and can't seem to drift off.
On days when you do not have to wake up for work, what time do you naturally start feeling sleepy enough to fall asleep?

I don't really have a set time, honestly. Since my schedule is so all over the place with the night shifts, I don't think my body even knows when it's supposed to be tired anymore. Even on my days off, I just feel that same constant exhaustion, but I couldn't tell you a specific hour when I naturally feel ready to sleep. It's just a blur.
When you have several days without work or an alarm, do you still lie awake for a long time before falling asleep?

Yeah, I do. Like I mentioned a minute ago, my sleep has just been messed up for a long time now. It doesn't really matter if I have a few days off in a row. After working those overnight shifts, I'll just lie there in bed... tired but wired, you know? And even if I eventually fall asleep and get a decent number of hours, I still wake up feeling like I barely rested at all. Having days off doesn't seem to reset it.
In a typical week, on how many nights do you lie awake for a long time before falling asleep?

I don't know exactly how many nights. It feels like almost all of them, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of a specific number, but it's definitely most nights out of the week that I'm just lying there, waiting to fall asleep.
After a night when you feel you slept well and wake feeling rested, do you still have the same difficulty concentrating during the day?

Yeah, it doesn't really seem to make a difference how I sleep. Honestly, that's kind of why I came in... my head just doesn't stay on task anymore. Like, I'll be doing inventory at work or trying to study for this supervisor certification I want, and I just keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk all the way to the supply closet and completely forget what I went in there for. It just happens all the time now, no matter if I slept okay or not.
What is the longest period you have had only daytime shifts, and during that period did you still have trouble falling asleep?

I honestly don't think I've had a period of just daytime shifts. I've been on the overnight cleaning crew for years now. So... I'm not really sure. I haven't had a stretch of normal day hours to compare it to, so I couldn't tell you if I'd still have trouble falling asleep or not.
After an overnight shift, when you try to sleep during the daytime, do you usually have trouble falling asleep?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, my sleep has been messed up for a really long time now. I'll get home from a shift and just lie there in bed... I'll be completely tired, but I just feel wired, you know? And the frustrating part is that even when I do manage to sleep a decent number of hours during the day, I still wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
During the longest stretch you have had a regular daytime schedule, did you still have trouble falling asleep at night?

Um, I think I just mentioned this, but I really haven't had a regular daytime schedule in years. It's just been the overnight cleaning shifts for a long time now. So I really couldn't tell you if I'd have trouble sleeping at night on a normal schedule, just because I haven't had a stretch like that to compare it to.
Before your work schedule changed to rotating evening and overnight shifts, did you regularly have trouble falling asleep at night?

I haven't ever worked rotating evening and overnight shifts. Like I said, I've just been on the overnight cleaning crew for years. So, I don't really know how to answer that. My schedule hasn't changed like that.
How sleepy do you feel while working your overnight shifts?

I don't really get that sleepy while I'm actually working. I mean, I'm on my feet most of the night, moving around and cleaning, so that keeps me pretty awake. I haven't really noticed having a hard time staying awake during the shift, if that's what you mean. It's really just when I get home that the sleep issues start.
Have you ever had at least two weeks away from overnight shifts, and during that time did you still have trouble falling asleep?

No, I haven't. I don't think I've taken two straight weeks off from work in... well, years. So I haven't really had a break away from the night shifts to see if my sleep would go back to normal. It's just been the same schedule straight through.
When you have a day off and do not set an alarm, what time do you usually end up falling asleep?

I'm not really sure, honestly. Even on my days off, I don't usually just let myself sleep whenever without an alarm. I try to keep somewhat of a schedule, so I haven't really tested what time I'd naturally fall asleep if I just left it open like that.
When you are able to sleep at the time your body naturally prefers, rather than during the daytime after an overnight shift, do you generally fall asleep and stay asleep without difficulty?

I'm really not sure. Like I mentioned, I haven't been off this night schedule in years, so... I don't even know what my body naturally prefers at this point. I haven't had a chance to just sleep a normal nighttime schedule to see if I'd fall asleep and stay asleep without any trouble. So I really couldn't tell you.
